learning_outcomes.text: Will know the fundamentals and basic applications of Technical Thermodynamics, its laws and principles, knowing how to apply them to practical situations.

Will know and master all fundamental and technical thermodynamic concepts, their representation, control, optimization and development, mastering the necessary computer tools and their mathematical and scientific foundations.
Will solve problems and practical situations related to various classic thermodynamic processes, including heat, cold, power generation, and mixed systems.
Will master the basic concepts and potential of exergy, knowing the fundamentals of exergoeconomic analysis and its applications in Thermal Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and fundamental concepts of Thermodynamics
Introduction and brief historical summary of thermodynamics
The First Principle in closed systems
The First Principle in open systems. Enthalpy.
The First Principle in cyclic processes: The heat engine, refrigeration cycle, and heat pump
State surface of a pure substance
Specific internal energy and enthalpy. Thermodynamic tables.
Thermodynamic processes with ideal gases. Ideal gas tables.
The First Principle of Thermodynamics in open systems
Conservation of mass and energy in a control volume
Mass and energy balances in steady state
Study of different devices in which open processes are carried out
The Second Principle of Thermodynamics. Entropy.
Clausius and Kelvin-Planck formulations of the Second Principle of Thermodynamics
Definition of entropy and Second Principle of Thermodynamics
Entropy balance in closed systems and control volumes
Transformation of heat into work through a cyclic process
Evaluation of thermodynamic processes with the help of exergy
Humid air: relative humidity and mixture enthalpy
Conservation of mass and energy in psychrometric systems
Adiabatic saturation: dry bulb and wet bulb temperature.
Mixture composition: mass and mole fractions and apparent molecular weight.
Conservation of energy in chemical reactions and thermochemical laws
assessment_rules: In the written exam, students who do not obtain 30% of the score will not be able to pass the course. If this critical criterion is not met, the total grade for the course will be FAIL, with the resulting grade from the sum of the scores obtained in all evaluation systems, truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points.
